briefdescription.para: The main entry to the graph construction algorithm.

detaileddescription.para: It starts by creating nodes in increasing order of granularity and then adds def-use and memory edges. As one of the final stages, it also creates pi-block nodes to facilitate codegen in transformations that use dependence graphs.

The algorithmic complexity of this implementation is O(V^2 * I^2), where V is the number of vertecies (nodes) and I is the number of instructions in each node. The total number of instructions, N, is equal to V * I, therefore the worst-case time complexity is O(N^2). The average time complexity is O((N^2)/2).

briefdescription.para: Compute ordinal numbers for each instruction and store them in a map for future look up.

detaileddescription.para: These ordinals are used to compute node ordinals which are in turn used to order nodes that are part of a cycle. Instruction ordinals are assigned based on lexical program order.

briefdescription.para: Create fine grained nodes.

detaileddescription.para: These are typically atomic nodes that consist of a single instruction.

briefdescription.para: Analyze the def-use chains and create edges from the nodes containing definitions to the nodes containing the uses.

Create a root node and add edges such that each node in the graph is reachable from the root.
Apply graph abstraction to groups of nodes that belong to a strongly connected component of the graph to create larger compound nodes called pi-blocks.

detaileddescription.para: The purpose of this abstraction is to isolate sets of program elements that need to stay together during codegen and turn the dependence graph into an acyclic graph.

memberdef.name: simplify

briefdescription.para: Go through all the nodes in the graph and collapse any two nodes 'a' and 'b' if all of the following are true:

listitem.para: the only edge from 'a' is a def-use edge to 'b' and
the only edge to 'b' is a def-use edge from 'a' and
there is no cyclic edge from 'b' to 'a' and
all instructions in 'a' and 'b' belong to the same basic block and
both 'a' and 'b' are simple (single or multi instruction) nodes.
